articles.author: Amir
articles.description:
I had studied:
arrays and objects
loops and conditionals
destructuring
string methods
even map, filter, reduce



But every time I opened a “simple” problem, my brain froze.
Not because of syntax.

Because I didn’t know how to think.
I was asking:
“What code should I write?”
Instead of:
What is the input?
What shape should the output have?
Am I counting, grouping, or transforming data?
Should the result be {} or []?
That single question — {} or [] — blocked me more times than syntax errors ever did.
I stopped rushing to write code.
Before touching the keyboard, I started writing this in plain English:
“I need to group items by X”
“I need to count how many times Y appears”
“I need one value per key”
Only then did loops, accumulators, and dynamic keys make sense.
_What was the moment JavaScript finally “clicked” for you?






js
const result = {};

for (const item of data) {
  const key = item.type;
  result[key] = (result[key] ?? 0) + 1;
}
articles.title: I thought I knew JavaScript.

articles.author: Geremi Wanga
articles.description:
🪐 Building an LLM Called Space


Lately, I’ve been working on an LLM called Space.
Not space as in rockets and physics.

More like quiet, dark, floating, breathe space.
The idea is simple:
A calm place to talk when your mind feels noisy.
A lot of tools want you to be productive.

Space wants you to be present.
No dashboards screaming at you.

No “optimize your feelings” energy.
Just you…

and stars slowly passing by.
Yes the entire app has an MP4 of stars drifting in the background, because if you’re going to overthink, you might as well do it in deep space 🌠
I’m finishing up the frontend in Angular, and instead of typical “AI features” like code review or text summarization, I leaned into something more emotional.
Some of the components so far:
Gentle Reflection


Help me put what’s on my mind into words
Emotional Check In


Help me understand how I’m feeling right now
Grounding Moment


Help me slow down and feel present
Self Compassion


Help me talk to myself more kindly
Each template is less of a command

and more of an invitation to pause.

(because typing is sometimes too much)
voice input modal that opens when you click the mic:




A calm message: “Click the microphone to start speaking”


A live transcript area: “What you say appears here…”


A Stop button


A Use Transcript button



Because sometimes you don’t want to “prompt” an AI you just want to talk.

File upload is wired up to the point where:
You can select files from your device


They’re picked up internally


Next step is deeper processing




Space isn’t trying to replace therapists or professionals.
It’s more like:
a quiet notebook that listens


a soft voice when you don’t have one


a place to untangle thoughts without being judged



Sometimes people don’t need answers.
space.
This is very much a work in progress but it’s one of those projects that feels personal in a good way.
If you’re building tech that:
humanity over hype
And if you’re not… that’s okay too.
space
articles.title: 🚀 Building Space: a calm Angular UI for an LLM (with stars)

Overview


Today, I'll launch a basic EC2 instance in the VPC we created in Day1 and connect to it.
To access EC2 by using SSM Manager, you need to attach 'AmazonSSMManagedInstanceCore' permission to the instance.

Create security group for EC2 by using the following settings.

AMI: Amazon Linux 2023




Systems Manager → Session Manager → Start session → run the following commands
whoami #check user name
uname -a #get system information
curl -I https://aws.amazon.com #check the connection to AWS domain


If you see a valid response, you've successfully launched the instance and connected to it via Session Manager.
Terminate the EC2.
Key exam points related to today's services.
There are four ways to access EC2.
SSM: connect to the instance without opening inbound SSH/RDP ports. should install SSMAgent in the instance (Most AWS-provided AMIs (e.g., Amazon Linux) include the SSM agent) and attach IAM role with SSM permission to the instance. ← today's hands-on!
SSH or RDP: use client softs like Teraterm and use keypair for Linux. use RDP and Administrator's password for Windows. should manage password or key pair by yourself. ← I'll try in tomorrow's hands-on!
EC2 Instance Connect: Connect to the instance via SSH using a public key with a short validity period (You shouldn't manage SSH key by yourself). should install EC2 instance connect in the instance.

EC2 Serial Console: connect to the virtual serial port of the instance. can connect to the instance doesn't have Internet connection, so useful for troubleshooting.
see you soon in the Day3 hands-on!
articles.title: DAY2 -EC2 + Remote access
